Dataset catalogue publication, licensing negotiation, DOI minting and distribution management for collections of observations
Downstream analytics, model assimilation, forecasting and statistical inference beyond recording that a result was derived
Sensor tasking, actuation and control commands
Laboratory quality-management-system scope, accreditation status and personnel competence records
Transport-level streaming guarantees, message ordering, delivery semantics and API pagination

boundary_notes.distinction: OMS and SOSA separate the Sample (a feature used to represent another feature) from the Observation (the act). This model carries the reference from the observation to its proximate feature of interest and, where that is a sample, to the sample identifier and the ultimate feature it stands for. Sample identity, sampling act, preparation steps, sub-sampling relationships and custody remain owned by the sample model.

OMS requires an observation to name exactly one ObservableProperty, and QUDT separates QuantityKind from Unit. This model holds the reference and any observation-specific constraint or qualifier on the measurand; it does not define the property term, its dimension, its synonyms or its deprecation policy.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Unit of Measure Registry (UCUM / SI / QUDT)
boundary_notes.distinction: UCUM and QUDT are governed unit code systems. This model records which code system and code express the result, and any observation-level scaling; it never redefines units, conversion multipliers or dimensional vectors, and it must not silently convert values.

SOSA defines Procedure as a workflow, protocol, plan, algorithm or computational method, and OMS makes the ObservingProcedure a first-class feature. This model records which procedure version was executed and the execution-specific parameters; method authoring, validation and approval belong to the method model.

OMS models Observer, Host and Deployment (with deploymentReason and deploymentTime) as separate features. This model references the observer and the deployment in force at the time of the act; asset lifecycle, platform management and deployment scheduling stay outside.

VIM defines metrological traceability as a documented unbroken chain of calibrations. This model records the traceability declaration and pointers to the calibration evidence in force; it does not model the calibration act, the reference standard hierarchy or accreditation validity.

QARTOD publishes QC test procedures and flag conventions; SensorThings exposes resultQuality as a recorded property. This model stores the resulting flag, the identifier of the test and the identifier of the evaluating agent. Rule authoring, threshold configuration, execution and re-evaluation are owned by the quality-control model and never by this one.

MHRA GxP data-integrity expectations place audit trail, tamper-evidence and signature control on the records system. This model requires that a record be linkable to its audit entries and preserves the original acquisition record as an artifact, but it does not define, generate, secure or query the audit trail itself.

DCAT governs Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService, with licensing, access rights and versioning at dataset level. This model records membership pointers from an observation to the collection, datastream or series that contains it; catalogue-level metadata, distribution management and publication workflow stay in the catalogue model.

SensorThings binds unitOfMeasurement and observationType at Datastream level, and the OGC Timeseries Profile defines series-level defaults such as interpolationType. Series-level defaults are referenced here so a single record remains interpretable in isolation, but the series aggregate owns its own identity, extent, default resolution and completeness accounting.

This model records which retention policy applies, the disposition decision and the tombstone it leaves behind. Policy authoring, legal-hold determination and the physical execution of destruction are owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy.

sources.title: Observations, Measurements, and Samples (OMS)
sources.version_or_date: OMS version 3.0, OGC Abstract Specification Topic 20 (OGC 20-082r4), published jointly as ISO 19156:2023
sources.relevance: Defines the normative conceptual schema for observations, for the features involved in the observation process and for sampling features, including sample typing by spatial, material and statistical nature and relationships between samples. Anchors the scope and top-level structure of this model.

sources.title: OMS Abstract Specification feature catalogue input (opengeospatial/om-swg)
sources.organization: Open Geospatial Consortium (OMS Standards Working Group)
sources.version_or_date: Working feature catalogue, draft status, dated 2021-08-20 in the document header
sources.relevance: Working OGC material listing the OMS classes and their properties: Observation (phenomenonTime, resultTime, validTime, resultQuality, parameter, observedProperty, observer, observingProcedure, proximate and ultimate featureOfInterest, result, relatedObservation), ObservableProperty, Observer, ObservingProcedure, Deployment (deploymentReason, deploymentTime, host), Sample (sampleType, sampledFeature, sampling, preparationStep, relatedSample) and Host. Explicitly working-draft; multiplicities must be re-verified against the published standard.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SOSA/SSN), 2023 Edition
sources.version_or_date: 2023 Edition; namespace http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/, version IRI http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/2023/; document state as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: Provides the lightweight core vocabulary for Observation, Sample, Sampling, Sampler, FeatureOfInterest, ObservableProperty, Procedure, Platform, System and Deployment, with hasResult, hasSimpleResult, resultTime, phenomenonTime, madeBySensor, usedProcedure, isSampleOf and hasUltimateFeatureOfInterest, plus the system-capability and operating-conditions module used for context of applicability.

sources.title: OGC SensorThings API Part 1: Sensing, Version 1.1 (OGC 18-088)
sources.relevance: Concrete normative realisation of the observation model with Thing, Location, HistoricalLocation, Datastream, Sensor, ObservedProperty, Observation and FeatureOfInterest. Supplies Observation properties phenomenonTime, result, resultTime, resultQuality, validTime and parameters, and the Datastream-level unitOfMeasurement, observationType and observedArea used to justify series-level versus record-level binding.

sources.title: OGC Timeseries Profile of Observations and Measurements (OGC 15-043r3)
sources.relevance: Establishes that correct machine interpretation of a value requires interpolation type, point versus interval or accumulation semantics, aggregation duration, cumulative flags, qualifiers, censored reason and nil-reason handling, plus series-level defaults. Grounds the aggregation, interpolation and censoring findings.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the provenance vocabulary used as an alignment: Entity, Activity and Agent with wasGeneratedBy, used, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime and endedAtTime, plus the qualified pattern (Generation, Derivation, Attribution, Association, Usage) for recording responsibility and derivation of an observation.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile requiring an explicit stated offset to UTC (Z or numeric offset), defining seconds and optional fractional seconds, the -00:00 convention for an unknown local offset, leap-second handling and the conditions under which timestamps sort as strings. Governs every temporal value in this model.

sources.title: JCGM Publications: Guides in Metrology (JCGM 100:2008 GUM; JCGM 200:2012 VIM; JCGM 106:2012; JCGM GUM-6:2020)
sources.organization: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures / Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
sources.version_or_date: JCGM 100:2008 (with Amd.1:2026), JCGM 101:2008, JCGM 102:2011, JCGM 106:2012, JCGM 200:2012, JCGM GUM-1:2023, JCGM GUM-6:2020; publications page as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: Authoritative vocabulary and method for measurand, measurement result, measured quantity value, standard and expanded measurement uncertainty, coverage interval and coverage probability, metrological traceability, calibration, measurement procedure, influence quantity, detection limit, trueness and precision, and for the role of measurement uncertainty in conformity assessment.

sources.title: The Unified Code for Units of Measure (UCUM) Specification
sources.organization: Regenstrief Institute, Inc. and the UCUM Organization
sources.relevance: Machine-oriented unit code system built for electronic data interchange, with case-sensitive and case-insensitive symbol forms over 7-bit US-ASCII and compound expressions with multiplication and division operators. Used as the default unit-code binding and as evidence that a unit binding must name its code system.

sources.title: QUDT Ontologies (Quantities, Units, Dimensions and Data Types)
sources.relevance: Separates QuantityKind, Unit, Quantity, QuantityValue, Dimension Vector and System of Units, with conversion multipliers and offsets and applicable-unit relations. Justifies modelling quantity kind and unit as two distinct bindings rather than a single free-text unit string.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Observation resource
sources.relevance: An independent, widely deployed observation model used as an alignment and counterexample source: identifier, status (registered, preliminary, final, amended), category, code (1..1), subject, focus, effective[x], issued, performer, value[x], dataAbsentReason, interpretation, method, specimen, device, referenceRange, hasMember, derivedFrom and component. Grounds record status, absent-reason, interpretation, composite results and member relationships.

sources.title: ILAC Guidance Series (ILAC-G8:09/2019 Guidelines on Decision Rules and Statements of Conformity; ILAC-G17:01/2021 ILAC Guidelines for Measurement Uncertainty in Testing)
sources.relevance: Normative accreditation guidance requiring that a statement of conformity identify the results it applies to, the specification met or not met, and the decision rule applied, and requiring documented evaluation and reporting of measurement uncertainty under ISO/IEC 17025:2017. Grounds the conformity and uncertainty findings.

sources.title: 'GXP' Data Integrity Guidance and Definitions
sources.organization: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (UK)
sources.version_or_date: Published 9 March 2018; last updated 27 September 2021; notes that the OECD Advisory Document on Data Integrity (September 2021) takes precedence for GLP facilities
sources.relevance: Regulator statement of data-integrity expectations across the regulated lifecycle, covering original records and true copies, contemporaneous capture, audit trail, and retention and archiving. Grounds the original-acquisition-record artifact, the amendment rules and the retention and disposition finding, while leaving audit-trail machinery to the records system.

sources.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) - Version 3
sources.relevance: Defines Dataset, DatasetSeries, Distribution and DataService with temporal and spatial coverage, prov:wasGeneratedBy, dcat:qualifiedRelation, versioning (hasVersion, previousVersion), dcterms:accessRights, license and identifier. Used to place catalogue-level publication, licensing and versioning outside this model while retaining membership and access-rights references.

sources.title: QARTOD - Quality Assurance / Quality Control of Real Time Oceanographic Data
sources.organization: NOAA U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System (IOOS)
sources.version_or_date: Programme active since 2003; Manual for Oceanographic Data Quality Control Flags version 1.2 final; manuals for 14 core variables described as living documents
sources.relevance: Public-authority evidence that quality flags are a distinct, documented, test-driven layer over a value: primary flags (pass, not evaluated, suspect, fail, missing), separate real-time and delayed-mode regimes, and per-variable test manuals. Grounds the quality-flag finding and the separation of flag recording from flag evaluation.

sources.title: WIGOS Metadata Guidelines for Data Providers (wmo-im/et-acdm wiki, referencing WMO-No. 1192 and schemas.wmo.int/wmdr)
sources.organization: World Meteorological Organization (Expert Team on Metadata, Information Management)
sources.version_or_date: WMO-No. 1192 WIGOS Metadata Standard cited as the published standard; wiki page as retrieved 2026-09-03
sources.relevance: First-party WMO working guidance confirming that observational metadata is organised into categories covering station and facility characteristics, deployments and instruments with begin and end dates, data quality and processing, ownership and data policy, and contacts, and that different organisations are the authoritative source for different categories. Used for the ownership, environment and data-policy findings; the standard text itself was not read and this is recorded as an evidence gap.

bundles.name: Observation Act and Identity
bundles.description: Establishes what one observation record is: how it is identified and versioned, how it is classified, and how it binds to the procedure execution and the executing observer that produced it.
bundles.rationale: OMS and SOSA both define an Observation as the execution of an observing procedure, not as a value. Any agent operating on such records must first resolve identity, kind and the act itself before it can interpret anything else; SensorThings and FHIR both make identity and a typed classification mandatory entry points.

layers.name: Record Identity and Kind
layers.description: Identity, versioning and classification of the observation record and of the act it documents.

findings.name: Observation record identity and version identity
findings.description: How a single observation record is uniquely and stably identified, how the identity of the record is distinguished from the identity of the observation act, and how successive versions of the same record are identified without colliding with new observations.

questions.text: Which system is the master system of record for this observation, and what identifier does it issue?
answer_data: Issuing system identifier and its role (LIMS, SCADA historian, observing service, clinical system)
Whether the identifier is guaranteed stable across export and re-import

questions.text: Is this identifier for the observation act or for the record that documents it, and how are the two related when one act yields several records?
answer_data: Relationship statement between act and record
Count of records documenting the same act

questions.text: How is a corrected or reprocessed version of this record identified relative to its predecessor?
answer_data: Whether the base identifier is retained across versions
Rule stating that a new version never reuses a superseded version identifier

questions.text: If no authoritative or governed identifier exists, what surrogate is minted and how is that fact recorded?
answer_data: Minting authority within the adopting Dimension
Flag marking the identifier as surrogate
Migration rule for when an authoritative identifier later appears

data_elements.name: observationIdentifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the observation record, resolved under the model identity priority.

data_elements.name: identifierScheme
data_elements.description: Name or IRI of the scheme, namespace or issuing authority that governs the primary identifier.

data_elements.name: alternateIdentifier
data_elements.description: Business or legacy identifiers carried alongside the primary identifier, each qualified by its scheme.

data_elements.name: recordVersion
data_elements.description: Version designator of this record, monotonic within the base identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is pure reference data: a set of identifier values, their schemes and their version relations. It has no rendered or stored form of its own, and materialising it as a document would create a second, competing source of truth against the master system that issues the identifier.

findings.name: Observation kind and result-type classification
findings.description: How an observation is typed so that an agent can predict the shape of the result and the applicable interpretation rules: the observation type or result type, the domain category, and whether the observation is direct, derived, simulated or estimated.

questions.text: What result type does this observation declare, and does the declared type match the actual result payload?
answer_data: Observation or result type code (measure, count, category, truth, complex, coverage, timeseries)

questions.text: Under which domain category or programme is this observation classified for discovery and rule selection?
Was the value obtained by direct determination, by derivation from other observations, by simulation or by expert estimation?
answer_data: Reference to source observations where derived
Justification note for estimated or simulated values

questions.text: Which observation profile or requirements class does this record claim to satisfy?
answer_data: Whether conformance was tested or only asserted

data_elements.name: observationType
data_elements.description: Code declaring the type of the result, controlling how the result payload is interpreted.

data_elements.name: domainCategory
data_elements.description: Domain or programme classification of the observation, drawn from a named vocabulary.

data_elements.name: determinationMode
data_elements.description: Whether the value was directly determined, derived, simulated or estimated.

data_elements.name: claimedProfile
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the observation profile the record asserts conformance to, with an explicit tested-or-asserted marker.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification consists of coded values drawn from external vocabularies plus a profile reference. The code lists themselves are owned by vocabulary and profile registries, so this finding carries codes and references only and produces no artifact of its own.

layers.name: Act and Procedure Execution
layers.description: The binding between the observation record and the procedure, observer, host and deployment that executed it, together with the execution-specific parameters in force.

findings.name: Procedure, observer, host and deployment binding
findings.description: How the record names the observing procedure that was executed, the observer or system that executed it, the host or platform carrying that observer, and the deployment in force at the time, each by reference to the model that owns it.

questions.text: Which observing procedure, at which version, was executed to produce this result?
answer_data: Procedure model or registry that owns the reference
Whether the executed version is still current

questions.text: Which observer, sensor, analyst or computational system carried out the procedure?
answer_data: Reference to the asset model entry, if any

questions.text: Which deployment of that observer onto which host was in force when the act occurred?
answer_data: Deployment time interval covering the act
Deployment reason recorded by the owning model

questions.text: Were there documented deviations from the procedure during this execution, and where is the deviation record held?
answer_data: Reference to the deviation or nonconformance record

data_elements.name: observingProcedureRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the procedure specification and version executed for this observation.

data_elements.name: observerRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the observer, sensor, analyst or computational system that executed the procedure.

data_elements.name: deploymentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the deployment of the observer on a host that was in force at the time of the act.

data_elements.name: procedureDeviation
data_elements.description: Recorded deviation from the procedure during this execution, with a pointer to the owning deviation record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Every element here is an outbound reference to a procedure, asset or deviation record owned by a sibling model. Reproducing those objects locally would duplicate their lifecycles; the record therefore stores only the reference, the version pinned at execution time and the deviation pointer.

findings.name: Observation parameters and influence quantities
findings.description: Named execution parameters and influence quantities that qualify the observation but are neither the measurand nor the result: settings, conditions applied, dilution or scaling factors, and any parameter needed to make the result reproducible.

questions.text: Which named parameters qualify this observation, and what value and unit does each carry?
answer_data: Parameter name and defining vocabulary reference
Parameter unit code and code system
Whether the parameter is mandatory for the declared procedure

questions.text: Which influence quantities were recorded or controlled because they affect the measured value?
answer_data: Whether it was measured, controlled or assumed
Reference to the correction applied, if any

questions.text: Which parameters are inherited from the series, datastream or method default rather than stated on this record?
answer_data: Source of the default (series, datastream, method)

data_elements.name: observationParameter
data_elements.description: Named value qualifying the observation act, each with name, value, optional unit and defining vocabulary reference.

data_elements.name: influenceQuantity
data_elements.description: Quantity that is not the measurand but affects the relation between indication and result, with its recorded value and control status.

data_elements.name: parameterInheritance
data_elements.description: Statement of which effective parameters were inherited from a series or method default and which were overridden on this record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameters are name-value-unit triples plus an inheritance statement. They are read and written as structured fields on the record, and the vocabularies that define parameter names belong to the property registry, so no separate artifact is warranted.

bundles.name: Subject and Property Binding
bundles.description: What was observed and on what: the feature of interest chain including any sample that stood in for it, and the observable property and measurand actually determined.
bundles.rationale: OMS requires an observation to name its feature of interest and exactly one observable property, and distinguishes the proximate feature (often a sample) from the ultimate feature the result is about. Misbinding either makes the result uninterpretable, so these are separated from the result itself.

layers.name: Feature of Interest Chain
layers.description: The proximate and ultimate features of interest and the sampling chain that connects them.

findings.name: Proximate and ultimate feature of interest
findings.description: How the record states the feature the result is actually about and, where observation was indirect, the intermediate feature that was directly observed, so that a result taken on a sample is never mistaken for a result taken on the whole.

questions.text: Which real-world feature is this result ultimately a statement about?
Which feature was directly observed, and does it differ from the ultimate feature?
answer_data: Indicator of whether proximate and ultimate differ
Kind of stand-in (sample, sampling location, proxy feature)

questions.text: On what basis is the proximate feature held to represent the ultimate feature, and what limits that representativeness?
answer_data: Reference to the sampling design or plan

questions.text: How is a feature reference resolved when the referenced feature is renamed, merged or split?

data_elements.name: ultimateFeatureOfInterestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the feature the observation result is ultimately about.

data_elements.name: proximateFeatureOfInterestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the feature that was directly observed, where different from the ultimate feature.

data_elements.name: representativenessBasis
data_elements.description: Statement of the basis on which the proximate feature represents the ultimate feature, with known limits.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding carries two typed references and a short justification statement. Feature entities, their geometry and their naming history are owned by the entity models being referenced, so materialising them here would duplicate another model's records.

findings.name: Sample linkage and sampling-chain reference
findings.description: How an observation made on a sample records which sample, where that sample sits in a sub-sampling or derivation chain, and which preparation steps had been applied before the observation, without absorbing the sample lifecycle.

questions.text: Which sample or specimen was this observation performed on?
answer_data: Reference to the sample model entry

questions.text: Where does that sample sit in the sub-sampling or derived-sample chain relative to the originally collected sample?
Which preparation steps had been applied to the sample at the moment of observation?
answer_data: Preparation step references in applied order
Preparation completion state at observation time

questions.text: Were there sample-condition findings that qualify the validity of this result?
answer_data: Sample condition code (for example haemolysed, degraded, contaminated, out of hold time)

data_elements.name: sampleRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the sample or specimen on which the observation was performed.

data_elements.name: samplingChainRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the parent sample and the relationship kind connecting it to the observed sample.

data_elements.name: preparationStateAtObservation
data_elements.description: Ordered references to the preparation steps completed on the sample before this observation.

data_elements.name: sampleConditionCode
data_elements.description: Coded condition of the sample that qualifies result validity, with a pointer to the owning condition record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The sample, its collection act, its preparation steps and its custody are owned by the sample model. This finding exists to pin the exact sample state that applied at observation time, expressed entirely as references and coded qualifiers, so it must not carry sample artifacts.

layers.name: Observable Property and Measurand
layers.description: The property observed and the fully qualified measurand, including the conditions that make the quantity intended to be measured unambiguous.

findings.name: Observable property binding
findings.description: How the record names exactly one observable property by reference to a governed vocabulary, distinguishes the property from its quantity kind, and handles properties that are only definable relative to a method.

questions.text: Which observable property term, from which governed vocabulary and version, does this observation determine?
What quantity kind underlies the property, and is it dimensionally consistent with the recorded unit?
answer_data: Consistency verdict against the recorded unit

questions.text: Is this property method-defined such that results from different procedures are not comparable?
answer_data: Procedure reference that defines the property

questions.text: Is the observed characteristic a quantity or a nominal property with no magnitude?
answer_data: Code list reference for nominal values
Consequence for unit and uncertainty requirements

data_elements.name: observedPropertyRef
data_elements.description: Reference to exactly one governed observable property term determined by this observation.

data_elements.name: quantityKindRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the quantity kind underlying the property, used for dimensional validation.

data_elements.name: methodDefinedProperty
data_elements.description: Indicator that the property is defined by its measurement procedure and is not comparable across procedures.

data_elements.name: propertyNature
data_elements.description: Whether the characteristic is a quantity or a nominal property without magnitude.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The property term, its label, its dimension and its governance all live in the vocabulary registry. This finding contributes only the pinned reference, the derived quantity-kind link and two discriminating flags, which are structured fields rather than a document.

findings.name: Measurand specification and stated conditions
findings.description: The quantity intended to be measured, stated completely enough to be unambiguous: the property, the feature or matrix it is measured in, and the conditions (temperature, pressure, basis, fraction, time base) under which it is defined.

questions.text: What is the complete statement of the quantity intended to be measured, including the conditions that define it?
answer_data: Measurand statement text or structured expression
Defining conditions with values and units

questions.text: On what basis is the value expressed (wet or dry, as-received, normalised, per unit mass, volume or area)?
answer_data: Whether the basis is a series-level default

questions.text: What definitional uncertainty arises because the measurand is not fully specified, and is it bounded?
answer_data: Whether it is included in the reported uncertainty

questions.text: Over what time base or integration window is the measurand defined?
answer_data: Whether it is instantaneous, averaged or accumulated

data_elements.name: measurandStatement
data_elements.description: Complete statement of the quantity intended to be measured with its defining conditions.

data_elements.name: expressionBasis
data_elements.description: Coded basis on which the value is expressed, including any normalisation reference.

data_elements.name: definitionalUncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty arising from incomplete specification of the measurand, with an indicator of whether it is included in the reported uncertainty.

data_elements.name: measurandTimeBase
data_elements.description: Integration window or time base over which the measurand is defined.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The measurand specification is a compact structured statement attached to the record. Where a fuller specification exists it belongs to the method document owned by the procedure model, so this finding deliberately holds the statement and its conditions inline rather than duplicating a method artifact.

bundles.name: Result, Quantity and Uncertainty
bundles.description: The result itself: its value and datatype, its unit and quantity binding, its absence or censoring, the uncertainty attached to it, the traceability that makes it comparable, and the interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SensorThings and FHIR all model the result as a typed slot that can hold simple, complex or absent values, while VIM and GUM require a measurement result to consist of a measured value together with information about its uncertainty. Separating value, unit, absence, uncertainty, traceability and interpretation prevents the common failure of storing a bare number.

layers.name: Result Representation
layers.description: How the result value is represented, dimensioned and qualified when it is missing or bounded.

findings.name: Result value, datatype and cardinality
findings.description: How the result payload is carried for simple scalars, categorical values, vectors, components, coverages, images and time-series blocks, including how the declared datatype constrains the payload and how multi-component results relate to their parent.

questions.text: What is the shape of the result payload, and which datatype governs its parsing?
answer_data: Payload shape (scalar, category, vector, component set, coverage, series block, binary object)
Encoding declaration for binary or structured payloads

questions.text: If the result has components, what is each component's property, value and unit, and can the parent be interpreted without them?
answer_data: Component list with property reference, value and unit
Component ordering rule where order is significant

questions.text: How many significant figures or what resolution does the recorded value carry, and is that a property of the value or of its rendering?
answer_data: Statement separating stored precision from display rounding

questions.text: For a large or binary result payload, how is the payload bound to the record and its integrity verified?

data_elements.name: resultValue
data_elements.description: The value determined by the observation, typed according to the declared observation type.

data_elements.name: resultDatatype
data_elements.description: Identifier of the datatype governing parsing of the result payload.

data_elements.name: resultComponent
data_elements.description: Component of a composite result, each with its own property reference, value and unit.

data_elements.name: recordedResolution
data_elements.description: Resolution or number of significant figures actually carried by the stored value, distinct from display rounding.

artifacts.name: Result payload object
artifacts.description: The stored payload of a complex or binary result that cannot be expressed as a scalar field: spectra, chromatograms, waveforms, images, point clouds, coverage grids or serialised time-series blocks. The payload is bound to the observation record by reference and digest, and is treated as read-only once the record leaves draft.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the payload locator issued by the storing system, qualified by the parent observation identifier and a zero-based part index where a result is split into ordered parts; a content digest is recorded so that identity can be re-established independently of the locator.

findings.name: Unit of measure and quantity binding
findings.description: How the unit of a quantitative result is recorded unambiguously by naming both the code system and the code, how series-level unit defaults are reconciled with record-level values, and why conversion is forbidden without recording it.

questions.text: Which unit code, from which unit code system and version, applies to the recorded value?
answer_data: Unit code system name and version (for example UCUM, QUDT, SI symbol set)
Case sensitivity form used where the code system distinguishes forms

questions.text: If the series or datastream declares a unit and this record declares another, which prevails and how is the conflict recorded?
Was the value converted from the unit in which it was originally determined, and where is that conversion recorded?
answer_data: Agent or system performing the conversion

questions.text: If no unit is recorded, is the result genuinely dimensionless or non-quantitative, and how is that asserted?
answer_data: Validation verdict rejecting silently missing units on quantities

data_elements.name: unitCode
data_elements.description: Unit code applied to the result value.

data_elements.name: unitCodeSystem
data_elements.description: Name and version of the unit code system that governs the unit code.

data_elements.name: unitBindingSource
data_elements.description: Whether the effective unit came from this record or was inherited from a series or datastream declaration, with the precedence rule applied.

data_elements.name: unitConversionRecord
data_elements.description: Record of any conversion from the originally determined unit, holding original value, original unit, factor, offset, rounding and responsible agent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit binding is a pair of coded references plus a conversion audit stub. The unit definitions, conversion multipliers and dimensional vectors are owned by the unit registry, and duplicating them locally would risk drift from the governed code system.

findings.name: Absent, censored and bounded results
findings.description: How the record expresses that no value exists, that a value is bounded rather than determined (below detection or quantitation limit, above range), or that a value was suppressed, so that absence is never encoded as zero or as an unexplained null.

questions.text: If no result value is present, what is the declared reason for its absence?
answer_data: Absence reason code (not performed, not applicable, error, withheld, lost, out of hold time)
Free-text explanation where the code is insufficient

questions.text: Is the value censored, and if so what is the bound, its direction and the limit that produced it?
answer_data: Limit kind (detection limit, quantitation limit, instrument range)
Reference to how the limit was established

questions.text: What rule must a consumer apply when aggregating or comparing a censored value?
answer_data: Substitution policy if any and its owner

questions.text: If the value exists but is withheld, what authority withheld it and under what condition may it be released?

data_elements.name: dataAbsentReason
data_elements.description: Coded reason a result value is absent from the record.

data_elements.name: censoring
data_elements.description: Censoring statement holding direction, bound value, unit and the kind of limit that produced the bound.

data_elements.name: detectionLimitRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the established detection or quantitation limit applicable to this procedure and matrix.

data_elements.name: suppressionMarker
data_elements.description: Marker that an existing value is withheld, with the withholding authority reference and release condition.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Absence and censoring are expressed as coded reasons, bounds and references to limits established by the method model. There is nothing to render or store as a separate object, and creating one would encourage treating a censored value as though it were a determined value.

layers.name: Uncertainty, Traceability and Interpretation
layers.description: What makes the result usable as evidence: its stated uncertainty, its metrological traceability, and any interpretation or conformity statement drawn from it.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty statement
findings.description: How the uncertainty associated with the reported value is stated so that it can be used: the kind of uncertainty, its value and unit, the coverage factor and coverage probability where expanded, and the basis on which it was evaluated.

questions.text: What kind of uncertainty is reported, with what numeric value and unit?
answer_data: Uncertainty kind (standard, combined standard, expanded, coverage interval)
Uncertainty value and unit or relative expression
Whether it is absolute or relative to the result

questions.text: For an expanded uncertainty, what coverage factor and coverage probability apply?
answer_data: Assumed distribution or effective degrees of freedom

questions.text: On what basis was the uncertainty evaluated, and which uncertainty budget or method does it come from?
answer_data: Evaluation basis (measurement model, validation data, proficiency testing, control chart)
Reference to the uncertainty budget owned by the method model
Whether contributions specific to this observation were added

questions.text: If no uncertainty is reported, is that a declared decision and on what ground?
answer_data: Ground for omission (not relevant to validity, not required for this result type)

data_elements.name: uncertaintyKind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of the reported uncertainty.

data_elements.name: uncertaintyValue
data_elements.description: Numeric uncertainty with its unit or relative expression.

data_elements.name: coverageParameters
data_elements.description: Coverage factor, coverage probability and assumed distribution or effective degrees of freedom for an expanded uncertainty.

data_elements.name: uncertaintyBudgetRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the uncertainty budget or evaluation method that produced the stated uncertainty.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The uncertainty attached to a single result is a small set of numeric fields plus a reference. The uncertainty budget itself is a method-level document owned by the procedure model; holding a copy here would create a second budget that could diverge from the validated one.

findings.name: Metrological traceability declaration
findings.description: How the record declares that the result is related to a stated reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, by reference to the calibration and reference-material evidence in force at the time of observation.

questions.text: To which stated metrological reference is this result traceable?
answer_data: Reference identifier (SI unit realisation, certified reference material, reference procedure, conventional scale)
Whether the reference is internationally recognised

questions.text: Which calibration of the observer or measuring system was in force when the observation was made?
answer_data: Calibration validity interval covering the act
Indicator of whether the act fell inside the validity interval

questions.text: Is any part of the traceability chain unestablished or broken, and how is that disclosed?
answer_data: Disclosure text carried with the result

questions.text: Which certified reference materials or reference measurements underpin the chain for this determination?
answer_data: Reference material identifiers and certificate references
Assigned value and its uncertainty as certified
Lot or batch identity where relevant

data_elements.name: metrologicalReference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the stated reference to which the result is traceable, with its issuing authority.

data_elements.name: calibrationInForceRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the calibration record valid at the moment of observation, with the covering validity interval.

data_elements.name: traceabilityChainCompleteness
data_elements.description: Statement of whether the traceability chain is unbroken, with any identified gap and its consequence for comparability.

data_elements.name: referenceMaterialRef
data_elements.description: References to certified reference materials underpinning the determination, with certificate references.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Calibration certificates and reference-material certificates are governed artifacts of the calibration and reference-material models, with their own issuance, validity and revocation lifecycles. This finding records only which of them were in force and whether the chain is complete, so it must not carry copies of them.

findings.name: Reference ranges, interpretation and conformity statements
findings.description: How a result is turned into a judgement: the reference range or specification limit it was compared against, the resulting interpretation code, and, where a statement of conformity is issued, the decision rule identifier and the risk basis behind it.

questions.text: Against which reference range or specification limit was this result compared, and for which population or condition does that range apply?
answer_data: Reference range or limit values with units
Source and version of the range or specification

questions.text: What interpretation was recorded for the result, and using which code list?
answer_data: Interpretation code (for example high, low, within range, out of specification)

questions.text: If a statement of conformity was issued, which decision rule was applied and where is it defined?
answer_data: Decision rule identifier and definition reference
Whether measurement uncertainty was taken into account and how
Guard band or acceptance limit applied
Specification or standard the statement refers to

questions.text: What level of false-accept or false-reject risk does the applied decision rule carry, and who accepted it?
answer_data: Stated risk level or probability of false acceptance
Whether the rule was requested by the customer or inherent in the specification

data_elements.name: referenceRange
data_elements.description: Reference range or specification limits used for comparison, with units and applicable condition.

data_elements.name: interpretationCode
data_elements.description: Coded interpretation assigned to the result, with its code list reference.

data_elements.name: conformityStatement
data_elements.description: Recorded statement of conformity naming the results it applies to and the specification met or not met.

data_elements.name: decisionRuleRef
data_elements.description: Identifier of and reference to the decision rule applied, including the guard band and stated risk basis.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The judgement recorded here is a set of coded values and references. The decision rule is defined and approved elsewhere, and the test report or certificate that publishes the conformity statement is a deliverable of the reporting model, so no artifact is created at the level of a single observation record.

bundles.name: Time, Place and Context
bundles.description: The temporal frame that makes a value locatable in time, the resampling semantics that make it safe to aggregate, and the spatial and environmental context in which it was obtained.
bundles.rationale: OMS, SOSA and SensorThings all separate phenomenon time from result time and admit a distinct valid time, and the OGC Timeseries Profile shows that a value cannot be correctly resampled without interpolation and aggregation semantics. SSN adds operating conditions as a context of validity. These are distinct decision surfaces and are grouped apart from the result.

layers.name: Temporal Frame
layers.description: The several distinct times attached to an observation and the semantics governing how the value behaves across time.

findings.name: Phenomenon, result, valid and ingestion time
findings.description: How the record distinguishes the time the observed phenomenon applies to, the time the result became available, the interval over which the result is asserted to be valid, and the time the record was captured or ingested, each with an explicit offset.

questions.text: To what instant or interval in the real world does this result apply?
answer_data: Phenomenon time instant or interval with explicit offset
Whether it is an instant or an interval
Precision or granularity of the stated time

questions.text: When did the result become available, and separately when was it captured into this record store?
answer_data: Ingestion or capture time with explicit offset
Whether ingestion time is system-assigned and immutable

questions.text: Over what period is this result asserted to remain valid for use?
What clock and offset were in force at the observing location, and how are local-time ambiguities resolved?
answer_data: UTC offset in force at the act
Time zone identifier where local civil time matters
Clock synchronisation source and known drift

data_elements.name: phenomenonTime
data_elements.description: Instant or interval in the real world to which the result applies, expressed with an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: resultTime
data_elements.description: Instant at which the result became available, expressed with an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: validTime
data_elements.description: Interval over which the result is asserted to be usable.

data_elements.name: ingestionTime
data_elements.description: System-assigned instant at which the record was captured into the store, distinct from result time.

data_elements.name: clockContext
data_elements.description: UTC offset and time zone in force at the observing location, with the synchronisation source and known drift.

findings.inline_only_rationale: All temporal context is a small set of timestamp fields plus a clock-context object. It is queried and compared as data, never rendered or exchanged as a standalone object, and materialising it would break the atomicity of the record.

findings.name: Aggregation, interpolation and sampling regime
findings.description: The semantics that determine how a value may be resampled, aggregated or compared: whether it is instantaneous, averaged, accumulated or cumulative, over what duration, and how interim values between observations may be inferred.

questions.text: Does this value describe an instant or an interval, and if an interval, over what duration was it aggregated?
answer_data: Statistical function applied (mean, maximum, total, count)
Alignment of the duration to the stated phenomenon time

questions.text: What interpolation type governs inference of values between this observation and its neighbours?
answer_data: Whether the type is inherited from the series default
Prohibition on interpolation where the type is undefined

questions.text: Is the value cumulative or a reset-prone running total, and what is the accumulation start reference?
At what nominal frequency or sampling regime was the series producing this observation operating?
answer_data: Deviation of this observation from the nominal regime

data_elements.name: aggregationDuration
data_elements.description: Duration over which the value was aggregated, with the statistical function applied.

data_elements.name: interpolationType
data_elements.description: Coded interpolation type governing inference of interim values, with the source of the code list.

data_elements.name: cumulativeFlag
data_elements.description: Indicator that the value is a running total, with the accumulation start reference.

data_elements.name: samplingRegime
data_elements.description: Nominal sampling interval and regime type in force for the producing series, with any deviation for this observation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are interpretation flags and durations carried on the record so that a single observation remains safely resamplable in isolation. The series that supplies the defaults is a separate aggregate with its own identity, so this finding holds effective values only and produces nothing storable.

layers.name: Spatial and Environmental Context
layers.description: Where the observation applies and under what conditions the observing system was operating.

findings.name: Observation location, geometry and spatial reference
findings.description: How the record states the position or extent the result applies to, distinguishing the location of the observer from the location of the feature or sample, and always naming the coordinate reference system and vertical datum.

questions.text: To what position or spatial extent does the result apply, as distinct from where the observer stood?
answer_data: Statement of which geometry the value is attributed to

questions.text: Which coordinate reference system, vertical datum and epoch express these coordinates?
answer_data: Coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic

questions.text: What positional uncertainty attaches to the stated geometry, and how was it obtained?
answer_data: Whether the position is measured, surveyed or nominal

questions.text: Was the location inherited from a station, site or sample record rather than measured for this observation?
answer_data: Effective date of the inherited position
Risk note where the source position may have changed

data_elements.name: resultGeometry
data_elements.description: Geometry or observed area to which the result is attributed.

data_elements.name: observerPosition
data_elements.description: Position of the observer at the time of the act, where it differs from the result geometry.

data_elements.name: spatialReferenceContext
data_elements.description: Coordinate reference system, vertical datum, coordinate epoch and axis-order convention for all geometry on the record.

data_elements.name: positionalUncertainty
data_elements.description: Uncertainty of the stated position with the positioning method that produced it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Geometry and its reference frame are structured values on the record. Station, site and sample geometry are owned by the corresponding entity models; this finding records what was effective for this observation and flags inheritance rather than storing a spatial document.

findings.name: Operating and environmental conditions of validity
findings.description: The conditions under which the observing system was operating and the environment surrounding it, which bound the applicability of any stated system capability such as accuracy, resolution or detection limit.

questions.text: Were the observing system's declared normal operating conditions satisfied at the time of the act?
What environmental context surrounded the observation and could plausibly bias the result?
answer_data: Environmental descriptors with values and units
Reference to the environment record owned by the station or facility model

questions.text: Under which validity context does the stated accuracy, resolution or detection limit hold for this observation?
answer_data: Whether this observation falls inside that context

questions.text: Was the system operating in a degraded, suboptimal or survival regime, and how is that disclosed with the result?
answer_data: Reference to the fault or maintenance record

data_elements.name: operatingConditionsAtAct
data_elements.description: Conditions under which the observing system was operating at the time of the act, with a within-range verdict against declared normal conditions.

data_elements.name: environmentalDescriptor
data_elements.description: Environmental descriptors surrounding the observation, each with value, unit and source.

data_elements.name: capabilityValidityRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the system capability statement and the validity context under which it holds for this observation.

data_elements.name: operatingRegimeCode
data_elements.description: Coded operating regime (normal, suboptimal, survival, degraded) in force during the act.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Capability statements, siting classifications and maintenance records belong to the observing-system and facility models. This finding contributes only the conditions effective at the act and the verdict against declared capability, which are fields on the record.

bundles.name: Quality, Validation and Lifecycle
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected, what quality judgements have been recorded against it, and who is responsible for it.
bundles.rationale: FHIR makes observation status a mandatory modifier element, QARTOD shows quality flagging as a documented layer distinct from the value, MHRA requires original records and controlled amendment, and PROV-O supplies the responsibility model. Together these form the trust surface of an observation record and are separated from the measurement content.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: The states an observation record can occupy and the controlled transitions between them.

findings.name: Record status and permitted transitions
findings.description: The lifecycle states of an observation record from provisional capture through review to final, amended, superseded or retracted, and the rules governing which transitions are permitted, by whom and with what evidence.

questions.text: What is the current lifecycle status of this record, and what does that status permit a consumer to do with it?
answer_data: Status code and its governing code list
Permitted consumer uses at that status
Whether the status is a modifier that changes result meaning

questions.text: Which transitions out of the current status are permitted, and what precondition does each require?
Who is authorised to move this record between statuses, and how is that authorisation evidenced?
answer_data: Separation-of-duties constraint where review is required

questions.text: Does this record represent a real-time provisional value or a delayed-mode reviewed value, and are both retained?
answer_data: Whether the provisional value is retained alongside the reviewed value
Reference linking provisional and reviewed records

data_elements.name: recordStatus
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle status of the record, drawn from a governed code list and treated as meaning-changing.

data_elements.name: statusTransition
data_elements.description: Record of a status change with source status, target status, instant, responsible agent and precondition satisfied.

data_elements.name: processingMode
data_elements.description: Whether the record is a real-time provisional value or a delayed-mode reviewed value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status and its transition history are coded fields on the record. The tamper-evident audit trail that independently attests to those transitions is owned by the electronic-records model, so this finding must record state without producing or claiming an audit artifact.

findings.name: Amendment, correction and supersession
findings.description: How a result that must change is handled: whether by amendment in place with a reason, by issuing a superseding record, or by retraction, always preserving the prior content and the reason for change.

questions.text: Which change mechanism applies to this record: amendment, supersession or retraction?
answer_data: Effect on the previous record's status

questions.text: What reason is recorded for the change, and is it classified as a correction, reprocessing or reinterpretation?
answer_data: Reference to the triggering finding or investigation

questions.text: How is the superseded content preserved and made retrievable after the change?
answer_data: Prohibition on obliterating the prior value

questions.text: How are consumers of the superseded value informed that it has changed?

data_elements.name: changeMechanism
data_elements.description: Coded mechanism by which the record's content was changed.

data_elements.name: changeReason
data_elements.description: Recorded reason and classification for the change, with a pointer to the triggering finding.

data_elements.name: supersedesRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the record version this one replaces, and the inverse pointer from the replaced version.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Amendment is expressed by a mechanism code, a reason and version pointers. The preserved prior content lives as an earlier version of the same record rather than as a distinct artifact, and downstream notification is executed by the distribution model, not here.

layers.name: Quality Assessment
layers.description: Quality judgements recorded against the observation and the evidence supporting them, recorded but never evaluated here.

findings.name: Quality flags and quality-control outcomes
findings.description: How quality judgements produced by external quality-control procedures are attached to the record: the flag value, the code list it comes from, which test produced it, when, and by which agent, without this model owning the tests or their execution.

questions.text: What quality flag is recorded against this result, and from which flag code list and version?
answer_data: Flag code list identifier and version
Whether the flag is primary or secondary level

questions.text: Which quality-control test or test suite produced that flag, and where is the test defined?
answer_data: Reference to the quality-control model that owns the test
Test outcome per test where a suite was run

questions.text: When was the flag assigned and by which agent or service?
answer_data: Flag assignment instant with explicit offset
Whether assignment was automated or manual

questions.text: When several flags disagree, which prevails for consumption and how is the disagreement preserved?

data_elements.name: qualityFlag
data_elements.description: Quality flag recorded against the result, with its value, code list, level and meaning.

data_elements.name: qualityTestRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the quality-control test or suite that produced the flag, with the parameters in force.

data_elements.name: flagAssignment
data_elements.description: Instant, agent and mode (automated or manual) of flag assignment.

data_elements.name: flagPrecedenceOutcome
data_elements.description: Prevailing flag after applying the precedence rule, with non-prevailing flags retained.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Flags are coded outcomes recorded on the record. Test definitions, thresholds, execution and re-evaluation belong to the quality-control model; carrying an evaluation artifact here would imply ownership of the evaluator, which this model explicitly does not have.

findings.name: Validation and verification evidence references
findings.description: How the record points to the evidence that supports its acceptance: control results, replicate or duplicate observations, blanks, spikes, proficiency-test outcomes and review sign-offs, each held by the model that owns it.

questions.text: Which control, blank, spike or replicate observations support the acceptance of this result?
answer_data: Whether each control passed its acceptance criterion

questions.text: Against which acceptance criteria was this result judged, and where are those criteria defined?
answer_data: Criterion values in force at the act

questions.text: Was the record reviewed and released, by whom and on what date and time?
answer_data: Pointer to the signature record held by the records system

questions.text: Was the procedure verified as fit for purpose in this laboratory for this matrix before the observation?
answer_data: Whether this observation falls inside the verified scope

data_elements.name: supportingObservationRef
data_elements.description: References to control, blank, spike or replicate observations that support acceptance of this result.

data_elements.name: acceptanceCriterionRef
data_elements.description: References to the acceptance criteria applied, with the values in force at the act.

data_elements.name: reviewRecord
data_elements.description: Reviewer reference, review instant and outcome, with a pointer to the signature held by the electronic-records system.

data_elements.name: methodVerificationRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the verification study establishing fitness for purpose, with the scope it covers.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Every item here is a pointer to evidence owned elsewhere: control observations are themselves observation records, acceptance criteria belong to the method model, and signatures belong to the electronic-records system. Materialising an evidence pack here would copy other models' records and create a second, unmanaged source of truth.

layers.name: Provenance and Responsibility
layers.description: Where the record came from, what it was derived from, and who is accountable for it.

findings.name: Provenance chain and derivation
findings.description: How the record states what generated it, which prior entities it used or was derived from, and how the original acquisition record is preserved so that the reported value can be traced back to what the instrument or observer actually produced.

questions.text: Which activity generated this record, and what did that activity use as input?
answer_data: Activity start and end instants with explicit offsets

questions.text: Which prior observations or entities was this result derived from, and by what transformation?
answer_data: Transformation or algorithm reference and version
Whether the derivation is reversible or lossy

questions.text: Where is the original acquisition record, and how is the reported value shown to correspond to it?
answer_data: Correspondence statement between original and reported value
Any processing applied between the two

questions.text: Has this record been reprocessed, and which processing version produced the current value?
answer_data: Prior processing versions and their outputs

data_elements.name: generatingActivityRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the activity that generated the record, with its start and end instants.

data_elements.name: derivedFromRef
data_elements.description: References to source observations or entities from which this result was derived, with the transformation applied.

data_elements.name: processingVersion
data_elements.description: Identifier of the processing version that produced the current value, with prior versions where reprocessed.

artifacts.name: Original acquisition record
artifacts.description: The original record captured at the moment of acquisition, in the form in which the observer or instrument produced it, retained unaltered so that the reported result can be traced back to it. Corrections never overwrite it; they create a new record version that references it.
media_or_form: transcribed field or bench sheet capture
true copy of an original record with its verification statement
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the acquisition-system record key (for example run, batch or injection sequence) qualified by the acquiring system identifier; where the acquisition system issues no key, a digest-addressed identifier is minted by the adopting Dimension and the parent observation identifier plus sequence position is retained as a composite fallback.

findings.name: Ownership, attribution and responsible agents
findings.description: Who owns the record, who is attributed as its producer, which organisation is the authoritative source for which part of it, and who may be contacted about it.

questions.text: Which organisation owns this record and is accountable for its correctness?
answer_data: Effective date of ownership and any transfer history

questions.text: To whom is the observation attributed, and does that differ from the owner?
answer_data: Difference statement between owner and producer
Delegation relationship where an agent acted on behalf of another

questions.text: Which organisation is the authoritative source for each part of the record when several contribute?
Who is the responsible contact for questions about this observation, and how is that contact kept current?

data_elements.name: owningOrganisationRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the organisation accountable for the record, with the effective interval of ownership.

data_elements.name: attributedAgentRef
data_elements.description: References to the agents to whom the observation is attributed, with their roles and any delegation.

data_elements.name: authoritativeSourceMapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from parts of the record to the organisation that is authoritative for each, with conflict-resolution rule.

data_elements.name: responsibleContactRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the contact record for enquiries about this observation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ownership and attribution are reference fields pointing at organisation, agent and contact records maintained by directory models. Copying those records here would duplicate an external register that changes on its own schedule.

bundles.name: Governance, Access and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record is protected and retired, how it is expressed for exchange without losing meaning, how its identifiers resolve across systems, and how it declares its membership in larger collections.
bundles.rationale: DCAT governs access rights, licence and versioning for published data; MHRA imposes retention and archiving duties; SensorThings, FHIR and OMS provide independent encodings that this model must be projectable into. These are governance and projection concerns, deliberately separated from measurement semantics so that storage and interface remain projections.

layers.name: Access and Retention
layers.description: Classification of the record for disclosure and its binding to a retention and disposition policy.

findings.name: Access classification and disclosure constraints
findings.description: How the record declares its sensitivity, the licence or access rights under which it may be used, and any constraint arising from personal, commercial or security sensitivity of the observation or its subject.

questions.text: What sensitivity classification applies to this record and to its result payload separately?
Under which access rights and licence may this observation be used and redistributed?
Does the observation identify or relate to an identifiable person, and what constraint follows?
Is the record embargoed or restricted for a period, and what releases it?
answer_data: Embargo indicator and expiry with explicit offset
Behaviour of derived products during embargo

data_elements.name: sensitivityClassification
data_elements.description: Classification of the record and, where different, of its payload, under a named classification scheme.

data_elements.name: accessRightsStatement
data_elements.description: Access-rights statement and licence identifier governing use and redistribution.

data_elements.name: personalDataIndicator
data_elements.description: Indicator that the observation relates to an identifiable person, with the applicable protection-regime reference.

data_elements.name: embargo
data_elements.description: Embargo state with expiry instant and releasing authority.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification, licence and embargo are declared values on the record. The policies that define the classification scheme and the enforcement point that honours them belong to the access-policy model; this finding must not imply that it enforces anything.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and tombstoning
findings.description: How long the record and its payload must be kept, which policy determines that, what disposition decision was reached, and what evidence remains after the record is destroyed.

questions.text: Which retention policy governs this record, and what retention period does it impose?
answer_data: Start event for the retention clock

questions.text: Do the record, its result payload and its original acquisition record carry different retention periods?
answer_data: Rule preventing payload loss while the record is retained

questions.text: Is the record under legal hold or another suspension of disposition, and who imposed it?
answer_data: Hold scope and expected review date

questions.text: What tombstone remains after disposition, and what may it disclose?
answer_data: Tombstone content specification (identifier, disposition instant, policy reference, authority)
Fields that must not survive disposition
Resolution behaviour for references to the destroyed record

data_elements.name: retentionPolicyRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the retention policy governing the record, with period and clock-start trigger.

data_elements.name: dispositionDecision
data_elements.description: Recorded disposition decision with instant, authorising agent and policy clause relied upon.

data_elements.name: legalHold
data_elements.description: Indicator and scope of any suspension of disposition, with the imposing authority.

data_elements.name: tombstone
data_elements.description: Minimal surviving record after disposition, carrying identifier, disposition instant, policy reference and authorising agent only.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding records the policy binding, the decision and the tombstone as data. The retention policy itself is authored by the adopting Dimension's records policy and the physical destruction is executed by the storage platform, so neither may be represented as an artifact owned here.

layers.name: Interoperability and Membership
layers.description: Alignment to external observation standards, resolution of identifiers across systems, and membership in collections and series.

findings.name: Standard alignment and encoding binding
findings.description: Which external observation standards this record is aligned to, which elements map cleanly, where mappings are lossy, and how the record is projected into a named exchange encoding without the encoding becoming the semantics.

questions.text: Which external observation standards and versions is this record aligned to, and is the alignment tested or asserted?
Which elements are lost, coerced or fabricated when projecting into each target encoding?
answer_data: Element-level mapping table with loss annotations
Fabrication risks (for example inferred per-observation units)

questions.text: Where do two aligned standards disagree about the same concept, and which is authoritative for this record?
Which encoding and profile was used for a given exchanged representation of this record?
answer_data: Instant of production with explicit offset

data_elements.name: alignmentDeclaration
data_elements.description: Declaration of each aligned standard, its version, alignment scope and whether conformance was tested.

data_elements.name: mappingLossNote
data_elements.description: Element-level note recording loss, coercion or fabrication in a projection to a target encoding.

data_elements.name: alignmentConflict
data_elements.description: Recorded disagreement between aligned standards over a concept, with the authoritative choice for this record.

artifacts.name: Encoded observation representation
artifacts.description: A concrete exchanged representation of the observation record in a named standard encoding and profile. It is a projection of the record, never its source of truth: it carries the encoding name, profile reference, producing agent and production instant so that a received representation can be traced back to the record state it was made from.
media_or_form: structured data document in a named observation encoding
message payload bound to a named profile
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent observation identifier combined with the encoding and profile identifier and the record version projected; a content digest is recorded so that a received representation can be matched to the exact record state that produced it.

findings.name: Identifier resolution and cross-system correlation
findings.description: How identifiers on and around this record resolve to the things they name, how the same observation is correlated across systems that assign their own keys, and how duplicate or conflicting records are detected and reconciled.

questions.text: How does a consumer resolve each identifier on this record to the entity it names?
answer_data: Whether the identifier is resolvable or opaque

questions.text: How is the same observation correlated when two systems have each assigned their own key?
answer_data: Reference to the accepted master identifier

questions.text: What constitutes a duplicate observation, and how is a duplicate reconciled rather than silently merged?
What happens when a referenced entity has been superseded, merged or destroyed since the observation was made?
answer_data: Whether the historical reference is preserved as recorded
Redirection or tombstone behaviour of the target

data_elements.name: identifierResolutionBinding
data_elements.description: Per-scheme statement of how an identifier resolves, whether it is resolvable and the fallback on failure.

data_elements.name: crossSystemCorrelation
data_elements.description: Correlation of this observation with keys assigned in other systems, with matching rule and confidence.

data_elements.name: duplicateReconciliationOutcome
data_elements.description: Outcome of duplicate detection, naming the retained record and the reason, without merging content silently.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Resolution bindings, correlation keys and reconciliation outcomes are reference data attached to the record. The resolvers, registries and matching services that operate on them are external systems whose behaviour this model describes but does not own.

findings.name: Collection, datastream and series membership
findings.description: How a single observation declares its membership in the collections, datastreams, series or composite observations that contain it, and which properties it inherits from them, without absorbing the containing aggregate's identity or completeness accounting.

questions.text: Which collection, datastream, series or dataset does this observation belong to?
answer_data: Position or ordering within the container where significant

questions.text: Which properties does this observation inherit from its container, and which does it override?
answer_data: Inherited property list with effective values

questions.text: Is this observation part of a composite or grouped observation, and can it be interpreted on its own?
If extracted from its container, does the record still carry everything needed to interpret the value?

data_elements.name: containerRef
data_elements.description: References to the collections, datastreams, series or datasets containing this observation, with kind and position.

data_elements.name: inheritedPropertySet
data_elements.description: Effective values inherited from the container, with overrides and the conflict-resolution rule applied.

data_elements.name: groupMembershipRef
data_elements.description: References to a parent or group observation and its sibling members where the result is part of a composite.

data_elements.name: standaloneCompletenessVerdict
data_elements.description: Verdict on whether the record remains interpretable when extracted from its container, listing any missing inherited elements.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Membership is expressed as outbound references plus the effective inherited values. The container aggregate has its own identity, extent, completeness accounting and publication lifecycle, so representing it as an artifact here would take ownership of another model's object.

functions.name: Register observation record
functions.description: Create a new observation record, resolve its identity under the model identity priority, and establish its initial lifecycle status and ownership.
inputs: Candidate master-system identifier and its issuing system
outputs: Registered observation record with a resolved primary identifier
Recorded identifier scheme and surrogate marker where applicable
preconditions: The issuing system is declared as the master system of record, or the absence of an authoritative identifier is explicitly asserted
The observation type is drawn from a named code list
An owning organisation reference resolves
effects: A durable record identity exists that later versions extend rather than replace
A surrogate identifier, where minted, is flagged so it can be superseded by an authoritative identifier later
No result content is asserted by this function alone

functions.name: Bind measurand and observation context
functions.description: Attach the mandatory referents that make the record interpretable: exactly one observable property, exactly one observing procedure, the ultimate feature of interest, and where applicable the proximate feature, sample, observer and deployment.
inputs: Observable property reference and vocabulary version
Ultimate and, where applicable, proximate feature of interest references
outputs: Bound measurand context on the record
Dimensional consistency verdict between property, quantity kind and unit
